notFound: Walmart Mexico and Bodega Aurrera (walmart.com.mx): the search page answered a 'Verifica tu identidad' bot-check page to curl and to a second fetch tool, so no listing was read; Atvio and Onn (Walmart house lines) therefore have no record (a search-engine result title names an Atvio 55 in model ATV5523KR at walmart.com.mx, but that page was not readable, so no model number or price was taken from it).

Philips: Liverpool's search for 'philips pantalla smart tv' returned 119 records and none is a television (remote controls and Hue light strips only), and Philips is not among the 30 brands in Cyberpuerta's TV filter, so no Philips TV price was confirmed.

Panasonic, Philco, Polaroid and Vizio: none is among the 30 brands in Cyberpuerta's TV filter or the 24 brands in Liverpool's filter for its 472-record TV category, and no other readable Mexican retailer page listed them, so no price was confirmed.
Coppel (coppel.com): the VTEX search API closed the connection (HTTP/2 INTERNAL_ERROR, then an empty reply over HTTP/1.1) and a second fetch tool got HTTP 503, so nothing was read.

Elektra (Incapsula challenge, HTTP 403), Soriana (Cloudflare 'Attention Required', HTTP 403), Sanborns (HTTP 403) and Office Depot Mexico (HTTP 503) refused the VTEX search request, so none of them was read.
Sears Mexico: the catalogue path answered the site's empty app shell (HTTP 200, no product data) and its data host seapi.sears.com.mx was not called, so no Sears listing was read.

Home Depot Mexico: its HCL search API answered HTTP 500 'CWXFS2002E Cannot connect to the search server' on three attempts with two endpoint forms and its search page is drawn in the browser, so no TV listing was read.

Costco Mexico, HEB and Famsa: the Costco search URL returned an app shell with no product data, and the HEB and Famsa catalogue paths returned ordinary HTML pages instead of a product feed, so none of them was read.

Liverpool: the Pantallas category (472 records, the first 56 read) and the Hyundai and Philips searches were read, but Hyundai, Daewoo, Aiwa, AOC, Toshiba and the other makers there are sold mostly by marketplace sellers (RANOR INFINITY, Electro Casa, Digimart and others) that are not recorded; only the two records whose sole seller is the maker's own store are kept (Hyundai HYLED5026QR sold by HYUNDAI ELECTRONICS MEXICO, Daewoo DAW32R sold by Daewoo TV) and their offer url is the listing page because the records carry no product-page link.

Chedraui: its Pantallas category lists 101 televisions, 51 from makers in scope and 48 recorded; left out are a JVC 55 in QLED Roku (id 3855488) and a Sharp 60 in 4K Roku LED (id 3876238) because their pages give no model number, and a JVC listed as 86 in with code SI70URF (id 3830960) because SI70URF is a 70 in model on Cyberpuerta, so title and code contradict.

Chedraui marketplace sellers (Doto, Endomex, Tienda Mercadazo) are not recorded, so Aiwa AW32B4SMRK has no Chedraui offer (Chedraui itself shows price 0 and no stock) and the Audiotek projection screens are not televisions.

Cyberpuerta: only the first page of JVC (16 of 19) and Sansui (16 of 18) was read, so 3 JVC and 2 Sansui listings are missing; the Hyundai, Daewoo, Sharp and Xiaomi brand pages and the Qtouch and BenQ brands were not opened (one Hyundai model appeared on the unfiltered page).
Cyberpuerta CHiQ 65 in 'U610M' is left out because the listing shows no full model number (the SKU is a barcode), while its 50, 55 and 75 in siblings carry 50U610M, 55U610M and 75U610M.

Prices: where a retailer shows a reduced price the regular (list) price is recorded and the reduced one is not (14 of the 48 Chedraui offers and both Liverpool offers carry a lower sale price), and Chedraui's list prices sometimes sit well above another retailer's price for the same model (Sansui SMX65KAUW 11,995 at Chedraui against 8,899 at Cyberpuerta); Cyberpuerta shows a single price, which is recorded.
Cyberpuerta marks 18 of the televisions recorded as out of stock when read; they are kept with the price shown.

Conflicting retailer text was settled thus: Hyundai HYLED5026QR (title FHD, description UHD and '4K') and HYLED4327QR (title UHD, long text both UHD and FHD) are recorded as 4K, HYLED5811R4KM (title '4K FHD', long text 'FHD') as 4K, HYLED3258QR (FHD at Chedraui, HD at Liverpool) as Full HD, HYLED6007QR (titled 'Led' but technology field QLED) as QLED, and HYLED5530 (sold as 'Mini QLED') as Mini-LED.

More settled conflicts: Sansui SMX43KAFW is Full HD (1920 x 1080) at Chedraui but HD at Cyberpuerta (Chedraui kept), Daewoo DAW40QRF is titled 40 in but its size field says 43 in (40 kept, matching the model code), Westinghouse WR43FX2212 is listed as 42 in (42 kept), JVC SI55URF and SI70URF are each listed twice on Cyberpuerta (the listing whose SKU equals the model number is kept), and Motorola MOT65UQE11 is listed twice (the in-stock listing is kept).

Fields left null because no page read states them: year and refreshHz throughout, resolution for Daewoo DAW32R and DAW40QRF, and smartOs wherever the listing does not name the system (every Cyberpuerta row except Xumo TV and Whale OS).

onModeWatts, powerBasis, powerUrl and eprel are null throughout because the energy label was not needed; Chedraui prints 'Consumo de energia' watt figures for many models but with no on-mode or SDR basis, and no EPREL number appeared on any page.

Six models share their model number with products already in tv-b.json (Insignia NS-43F501NA26, RCA TC-LE32K-AN2401, TC-LE43K-AN2401 and TC-LE50K-GO2401, Toshiba 50C350NU and 75C350NU), so their Mexico offers here should be merged into those products.
